purpose: baseline of 0.5.x / 0.6 (stored-result diagnostics; release gates use the interleaved A/B against the 0.5.0 source tree)
methodology: schema 2.2, Harness V3 (5 warm-ups, 3 x 7 batches, >= 50 ms per sample, median-of-medians), median of three complete runs (tools/ace-repeatability0.5.1.py), interleaved A/B vs the 0.5.0 source tree (3 batches per side, alternating order)

verdict.repeatability: pass, deterministic values identical; macro spread <= 5 % (compression) / <= 15 % (decompression, observed maximum 13.5 %)
verdict.ab_vs_0_5_0: pass, 12 / 12 cases, byte-identical output; speed ratios 0.961 - 1.011 (dense decode 0.961, fast / balanced encode 0.964 - 0.967, all others >= 0.978)

files: benchmark-0.5.1-<family>.json (27 families incl. regression and repeatability) and ab-0.5.1-vs-0.5.0.json, unchanged from the run
note: reference run of the 0.5.1 release on the author's workstation (performance governor, 35 - 37 C); the stored_baseline and lz4 / zstd drift rows are diagnostics against the 0.5.0 results. Known: dense decode and the fast / balanced / dense encode are 2 - 4 % slower than 0.5.0 (inside the 5 % gate), attributed to the stricter decoder checks and not yet profiled.
